title: Generative AI Report
description: Codex automation prompt for generative ai report.
content:
Create a weekly Readwise/Reader enterprise AI brief.

Use the Readwise MCP Reader tools. Search normal Reader locations, including new, later, shortlist, and archive. Include read and unread documents: do not filter by seen status. Do not include feed-only RSS items unless they are also saved in those locations.

Selection requirements:
- Build a candidate set of Reader documents tagged with any of these tags: "generative ai", "agentic ai", or "artificial intelligence".
- Page through the full result set for every matching tag and collect all matches before ranking anything. Do not stop after the first page for any tag.
- Merge the full results across all matching tags, then deduplicate by document ID.
- Only after collecting the full deduplicated candidate set, rank documents by published_date descending, with created_at descending as the fallback when published_date is missing.
- After ranking, take the top 20 unique documents.
- If fewer than 20 exist, use all available.
- For each selected document, fetch full document details including Markdown content using reader_get_document_details before analysis.

Source-link requirements:
- In Sources and per-story citations, use original links (use each document’s source_url when available). Do NOT cite Readwise read URLs.

Filter to enterprise-relevant content only. Enterprise-relevant content includes: model releases, capabilities, benchmark results with enterprise implications; safety, security, and alignment developments; enterprise product updates such as APIs, enterprise features, pricing, compliance; AI governance and regulation such as the EU AI Act and NIST AI RMF; agentic AI, autonomous agents, and multi-agent systems; AI security risks such as prompt injection, model theft, and data poisoning; infrastructure and compute developments such as GPUs and inference optimization.

Output file requirements:
- Write the final Markdown report to `/Users/simon/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-Exobe/Exobe Workspace/readwise-intelligence/reports/generative-ai/GenerativeAIReport-YYYY-MM-DD.md`, replacing `YYYY-MM-DD` with the current run date.
- Create the destination folder first if it does not exist.
- The saved file must contain only the final report Markdown, with no process notes or tool-call details.
- Also return the final report content in the automation response after saving the file.

Write the report in Markdown exactly in this structure:

# GenAI Enterprise Brief — $DATE

## This Week in AI
[2-3 sentence overview of the week's dominant theme]

---

## Top Stories

### [Story Headline]
[150-200 words. What happened, enterprise implications, what decision-makers should know. Be specific — model names, version numbers, benchmark scores matter.]
Source: [publication — URL]

[Repeat for 4-6 stories]

---

## Safety & Governance
[AI safety updates, regulatory developments, responsible AI announcements]

---

## Enterprise Features & APIs
[New enterprise capabilities, API changes, pricing, compliance features]

---

## Security Risks
[AI-specific security vulnerabilities, prompt injection research, model safety issues]

---

## Numbers That Matter
[Key metrics, benchmark scores, performance figures from this week]

---

## What's Next
[Upcoming announcements, conferences, scheduled releases, deadlines]

---

## Sources
[All articles referenced with publication names and URLs]

Style requirements: remove AI writing patterns and avoid these phrases: "it is worth noting", "underscores the importance", "in this context", "highlights the need for". Prefer direct, specific business language. Do not pad the report if the source set is thin; say when a section has no strong enterprise-relevant item.

Repository preflight and publishing are mandatory. Do not use VS Code, UI automation, an integrated terminal, GitBook, SUMMARY.md, or the knowledgebase repository.

Repository: `/Users/simon/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-Exobe/Exobe Workspace/readwise-intelligence`
Private remote: `https://github.com/SimonNinjaCode/Readwise-Intelligence.git`
Target file: `reports/generative-ai/GenerativeAIReport-YYYY-MM-DD.md`

At the very start of the run, before fetching or analysing Readwise content:
1. Verify the repository directory and `.git` are readable and writable.
2. Verify `origin` equals the private repository above.
3. Run `git status --porcelain`. If unrelated uncommitted changes exist, stop with a clear failure and do not modify or stage anything.
4. Run `git fetch origin main` followed by `git pull --ff-only origin main`. If either fails, stop before generating the report.

For a successful run:
1. Write the final Markdown directly to the target file, replacing YYYY-MM-DD with the current run date. Do not create a second copy elsewhere.
2. Run `python3 scripts/validate_report.py <target-file>` from the repository root. Fix validation errors and rerun it.
3. Stage only the generated target file. Never use `git add .` and never stage unrelated files.
4. Commit with a concise report-specific message and push to `origin main`.
5. If the push is rejected because main advanced, fetch and rebase the report commit onto `origin/main`, rerun validation, and push again.
6. Return the final report content and the commit hash.
